{
  "segment_function": "Discussing the ancient understanding of labor, slavery, and necessity, the distinction between the animal laborans and human freedom, and the modern reversal of these traditional rankings.",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The ancients despised labor and occupations serving life's maintenance because of their slavish nature, feeling it necessary to possess slaves to cope with this enslavement by necessity, rather than despising them merely because slaves performed them.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The opinion that labor and work were despised in antiquity because only slaves were engaged in them is a prejudice of modern historians. The ancients reasoned the other way around and felt it necessary to possess slaves because of the slavish nature of all occupations that served the needs for the maintenance of life.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "confidence": 1
    },
    {
      "claim": "The modern age glorified labor as the source of all values and elevated the animal laborans, yet failed to produce a clear theoretical distinction between animal laborans and homo faber.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "It is surprising at first glance, however, that the modern age—with its reversal of all traditions... should not have brought forth a single theory in which animal laborans and homo faber, “the labour of our body and the work of our hands,” are clearly distinguished.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "confidence": 1
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [],
  "distinctions": [],
  "examples": [],
  "objections": [],
  "responses": [],
  "references_to_other_sections": [],
  "unresolved_context": [],
  "must_not_be_lost": [
    "Slavery in antiquity was an attempt to exclude labor from human life rather than a device for cheap labor or profit exploitation.",
    "Aristotle's denial of the term 'men' to those totally subject to necessity referred to the usage of the species name rather than the slave's capacity to be human."
  ]
}
